intent.raw_query: Hawaii family beach vacation, $5000, 10 days, August 2026 from Seattle

selected_hotel.name: Hanauma Bay, East Oahu Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay
experiences.description: Explore one of Hawaii's most pristine marine sanctuaries with crystal-clear waters teeming with tropical fish and sea turtles. Perfect for families with kids of all ages, the bay offers calm, shallow waters and equipment rentals on-site. An educational orientation video is required before entering, making it a fun learning experience for the whole family.

experiences.name: Luau Dinner at Polynesian Cultural Center
experiences.description: Immerse your family in authentic Hawaiian and Polynesian culture with a spectacular beachfront luau featuring traditional hula dancing, fire knife performances, and an all-you-can-eat feast of local Hawaiian cuisine including kalua pig, poi, and fresh tropical fruits. A memorable cultural evening for the entire family.

experiences.name: Surfing Lessons at Waikiki Beach
experiences.description: Take beginner-friendly surfing lessons right on the iconic Waikiki shoreline with certified local instructors. The gentle rolling waves of Waikiki make it the perfect spot for first-timers and kids. Group lessons are available for families, and most participants are standing on a board within the first hour. Boards and rash guards are included.

experiences.name: Shave Ice and Local Food Tour in Haleiwa
experiences.description: Stroll through the charming beachside town of Haleiwa on the North Shore and indulge in Hawaii's most beloved treat — rainbow shave ice topped with local syrups and mochi. Sample fresh poke bowls, garlic shrimp from roadside trucks, and tropical smoothies. A delicious and affordable way to taste authentic Hawaiian flavors as a family.

experiences.name: Whale Watching Cruise from Maalaea Harbor
experiences.description: Embark on a family-friendly whale watching boat tour during peak humpback whale season off the coast of Maui. Knowledgeable naturalist guides narrate the experience as you witness majestic humpback whales breaching and tail-slapping just offshore. Many tours offer a money-back guarantee if no whales are spotted. Life jackets and snacks are provided on board.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Hawaii
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Hanauma Bay, East Oahu Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay
experiences.description: Explore one of Hawaii's most pristine marine sanctuaries with crystal-clear waters teeming with tropical fish and sea turtles. Perfect for families with kids of all ages, the bay offers calm, shallow waters and equipment rentals on-site. An educational orientation video is required before entering, making it a fun learning experience for the whole family.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Daniel K. Inouye International Airport at 13:00. Collect luggage, pick up a TheBus pass (affordable public transit) or arrange a rideshare to Hanauma Bay area (~30–40 min). Check in to the Hanauma Bay, East Oahu Boutique Stay. Freshen up and take a short orientation walk around the neighborhood to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Head to nearby Koko Marina Center for a relaxed first evening. Browse the shops, grab shave ice from a local stand, and enjoy the marina views. Keep it low-key after a long travel day.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a quick snack at the airport
meals.lunch: Grab a plate lunch from a food truck or L&L Hawaiian Barbecue near the airport before heading to the hotel (~$10–14 per person)
meals.dinner: Koko Marina Center — try Zippy's for affordable local comfort food like chili rice or saimin noodles (~$10–13 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Pick up a 7-day or multi-day TheBus pass at the airport or nearby convenience store to save on transportation costs throughout the trip. Stock up on snacks and water at a nearby Times Supermarket or Foodland to keep meal costs down.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay — Reserve your entry online in advance (required; $25/adult, free for Hawaii residents, children under 13 free). Arrive early (opens at 6:45 AM) to beat crowds. Watch the mandatory marine education video, then enjoy 2–3 hours exploring the stunning reef teeming with sea turtles, parrotfish, and tropical fish.
day_by_day.afternoon: After Hanauma Bay, walk or take a short drive to Koko Head Crater Trail for a challenging but rewarding hike up 1,048 railroad-tie steps. Views of the coastline and Diamond Head are spectacular. Free to hike.
day_by_day.evening: Relax back at the hotel. Enjoy a sunset from nearby Portlock Road coastal lookout, a hidden gem with dramatic lava rock coastline views.

meals.breakfast: Prepare a simple breakfast at the hotel using groceries (yogurt, fruit, granola bars) — budget ~$3–5 per person
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch to bring to Hanauma Bay (outside food allowed before entering the water area) — sandwiches, fruit, and snacks from the supermarket (~$5–7 per person)
meals.dinner: Kaimana Farm Café or a local poke bowl spot near Koko Marina — fresh poke bowls run ~$12–16 per person

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay entry must be reserved online at least 2 days in advance. Bring reef-safe sunscreen (required by Hawaii law), water shoes, and a reusable water bottle. Snorkel gear can be rented at the bay for ~$12.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Sandy Beach Park, just a 5-minute drive from the hotel. Known as one of Oahu's most powerful shore break beaches — great for watching experienced bodysurfers and boogie boarders. Swim with caution (strong currents); better for watching and sunbathing with kids.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or take TheBus along the scenic Kalanianaole Highway to Makapuu Point Lighthouse Trail (free). The 2-mile round-trip paved trail offers breathtaking views of the Windward Coast, offshore islands, and during August, possible humpback whale sightings. Family-friendly and stroller-accessible.
day_by_day.evening: Continue to Waimanalo Beach — one of Oahu's longest and most beautiful white-sand beaches. Free parking. Enjoy the calm waters for a late afternoon swim before heading back.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast prep — scrambled eggs, toast, and fruit from groceries (~$4 per person)
meals.lunch: Keneke's BBQ in Waimanalo — a beloved local spot with affordable plate lunches, laulau, and kalua pork (~$10–13 per person)
meals.dinner: Pick up groceries at Foodland Farms and cook a simple dinner at the hotel to save money (~$8–10 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Sandy Beach has a lifeguard but is notorious for injuries — supervise children closely near the water. Makapuu trail is exposed with little shade; bring hats, sunscreen, and plenty of water. August is peak season so arrive early at popular spots.

day_by_day.morning: Take TheBus or drive to Waikiki Beach (about 20–25 min from Hanauma Bay). Spend the morning on the world-famous beach — swimming, building sandcastles, and people-watching. Free beach access. Rent a bodyboard from a beach vendor (~$10/hour) for extra fun.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the Waikiki strip and visit Kapiolani Park — a large free public park with open lawns, a bandstand, and the Waikiki Shell. Visit the free Honolulu Zoo entrance area or simply enjoy the park. Head to the Duke Kahanamoku Statue for a photo op.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the free hula and Hawaiian music performances at Kuhio Beach Torch Lighting & Hula Show (Tues, Thurs, Sat evenings at 6:30 PM — check schedule). A wonderful, authentic, and completely free cultural experience.

meals.breakfast: Grab malasadas (Portuguese donuts) from Leonard's Bakery on the way to Waikiki — a must-try Hawaii treat (~$2–3 each)
meals.lunch: Waikiki — grab a plate lunch from a food truck or the Waikiki Market deli counter (~$10–13 per person)
meals.dinner: Marukame Udon in Waikiki — incredibly popular, budget-friendly Japanese udon restaurant. Expect a short line; meals start at ~$6–9 per person. Perfect for families.

day_by_day.notes: Parking in Waikiki is expensive ($3–5/hour). TheBus routes 22 or 23 connect Hanauma Bay area to Waikiki affordably. Keep valuables secured on the beach. The hula show is weather-dependent — check the City & County of Honolulu website for updates.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Diamond Head State Monument (about 15 min from hotel). Hike the iconic 1.6-mile round-trip trail to the summit crater rim for panoramic views of Honolulu and the Pacific. Entry is $5/person (or $10/car). Arrive by 7:00 AM to beat the heat and crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Kahala Mall area for a visit to The Kahala Hotel's public beach access — a calm, less-crowded beach perfect for families with young children. Free to access the beach. Alternatively, visit Waialae Beach Park nearby, also calm and family-friendly.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the East Oahu area. Visit the blowhole at Halona Blowhole Lookout (free, 5 min from hotel) at sunset for dramatic ocean spray and golden light views.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before the hike — oatmeal, bananas, and coffee from groceries (~$3–4 per person)
meals.lunch: Kahala Mall food court — affordable options including Panda Express, local bento shops, and more (~$10–12 per person)
meals.dinner: Ono Hawaiian Foods in Honolulu (a short drive) — an iconic, no-frills local restaurant serving authentic Hawaiian food like poi, lomi salmon, and haupia (~$12–15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Diamond Head trail involves a steep section with stairs and a tunnel — bring a flashlight or phone torch. The trail is paved but strenuous for young children; plan accordingly. Timed entry reservations may be required — check gohawaii.com in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the North Shore — take TheBus Route 55 or drive (~45–60 min). Start at Waimea Valley (entry ~$20/adult, $10/child). Walk the botanical garden trail through lush jungle to a stunning freshwater waterfall and swimming hole. A magical family experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Haleiwa Town on the North Shore — a charming surf town with galleries, boutiques, and local flavor. Visit Matsumoto Shave Ice, a legendary institution since 1951. Walk along the Haleiwa Beach Park shoreline.
day_by_day.evening: Stop at Sunset Beach or Ehukai Beach (Banzai Pipeline) on the drive back — in August the waves are calm and perfect for swimming (big waves come in winter). Watch the sunset before heading back to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Pack snacks and fruit from the hotel for the drive/bus ride
meals.lunch: Giovanni's Shrimp Truck in Haleiwa — a North Shore legend. Garlic shrimp plates are ~$14–16 per person and absolutely worth it
meals.dinner: Pick up fresh produce and protein from a Haleiwa farmers' market or Foodland on the way home and cook at the hotel (~$8–10 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The North Shore is about 45–60 minutes from East Oahu by car. TheBus is affordable but takes longer (~2 hours). Pack reef-safe sunscreen, water, and snacks for the full day. Waimea Valley is one of the best family-friendly nature experiences on Oahu.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Pearl Harbor National Memorial (about 35 min from hotel via H-1 freeway). The USS Arizona Memorial is free (reserve timed tickets online in advance at recreation.gov). The site is deeply moving and historically significant — a must-see.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the free outdoor exhibits at Pearl Harbor, including the USS Oklahoma Memorial and the historic anchor displays. Visit the nearby Battleship Missouri Memorial if budget allows ($32/adult, $16/child) or skip for free outdoor areas.
day_by_day.evening: Head back toward Honolulu for the Saturday Night Kaka'ako Farmers' Market at Ward Village — a vibrant local market with affordable food vendors, live music, and local crafts. Great family atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast prep — cereal, milk, and fruit (~$3–4 per person)
meals.lunch: Eat at Pearl Harbor's food concession area or bring a packed lunch (outside food allowed in picnic areas) (~$5–8 per person)
meals.dinner: Kaka'ako Farmers' Market food vendors — sample local dishes like poke, lumpia, and fresh fruit for ~$10–14 per person total

day_by_day.notes: Pearl Harbor entry is free but the boat shuttle to the USS Arizona Memorial is first-come, first-served or reservable online (small fee). Arrive early or book ahead. No bags larger than a small purse are allowed — leave backpacks in the car. This is a solemn site; prepare children appropriately.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Hanauma Bay for a second snorkeling session — now that you know the layout, you can explore deeper sections of the reef and spot more marine life. Alternatively, try snorkeling at Electric Beach (Kahe Point) near Ko Olina for a different experience with sea turtles and spinner dolphins (free, no reservation needed).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Ko Olina Lagoons (~40 min from hotel) — four man-made, calm, family-friendly lagoons perfect for young children. Free public access. Enjoy the calm turquoise waters and white sand in a resort setting without resort prices.
day_by_day.evening: Catch the sunset at Ko Olina — one of the best sunset spots on Oahu's west side. The lagoons face west and offer unobstructed ocean sunsets.

meals.breakfast: Acai bowl from a local café near the hotel — filling and nutritious (~$10–13)
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch from grocery store items to enjoy at Ko Olina Lagoon (~$5–7 per person)
meals.dinner: Stop at a Kapolei Town Center food option on the way back — Raising Cane's or Panda Express for affordable family-friendly dining (~$10–12 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Ko Olina lagoon parking is free but fills up fast on weekends — arrive before 9 AM or after 2 PM. Electric Beach is a local favorite for snorkeling and is less regulated than Hanauma Bay, but currents can be stronger. Best for confident swimmers.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Bishop Museum in Honolulu (~25 min from hotel) — Hawaii's premier natural and cultural history museum. Tickets are ~$26/adult, $19/child (look for online discount codes). Explore Hawaiian artifacts, a planetarium, and cultural demonstrations. Excellent for families.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Chinatown in downtown Honolulu for a cultural walkabout. Explore the Oahu Market, art galleries, and historic buildings. Visit the Foster Botanical Garden ($5/adult, free for children under 12) — a peaceful urban oasis with ancient trees and rare tropical plants.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through downtown Honolulu's waterfront area — Aloha Tower Marketplace. Enjoy the harbor views and browse the shops. Look for free live music events that often happen on weekend evenings.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — smoothies made with grocery-bought fruit and yogurt (~$3–5 per person)
meals.lunch: Chinatown — visit a local dim sum restaurant or noodle shop for an authentic, affordable meal (~$8–11 per person)
meals.dinner: Aloha Tower Marketplace food options or pick up a bento box from a local deli (~$10–13 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Bishop Museum is one of the best value cultural experiences in Hawaii — budget at least 2–3 hours. Chinatown is vibrant but watch belongings in busy market areas. Foster Botanical Garden is a hidden gem that most tourists skip — highly recommended for families.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at Hanauma Bay or Sandy Beach — one last swim and snorkel in Hawaii's beautiful waters. Collect any shells (no live animals or coral), take photos, and soak in the aloha spirit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head back to the hotel for checkout. Pack up and do a final grocery run for any local snacks and treats to bring home — macadamia nuts, Kona coffee, local honey, and Hawaiian sea salt make great affordable souvenirs. Drive or take TheBus to the airport (allow 45–60 min).
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Daniel K. Inouye International Airport. Arrive at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for international departures.

meals.breakfast: Use up remaining groceries from the hotel for a final Hawaiian-style breakfast — fresh pineapple, papaya, and toast (~$3–4 per person)
meals.lunch: Grab a final plate lunch from a food truck near the hotel or airport — kalua pork, rice, and macaroni salad (~$10–13 per person)
meals.dinner: Airport dining — Island Brew Coffeehouse & Kitchen or local options inside the terminal (~$13–18 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 11 AM — confirm with the hotel. Luggage storage may be available if your flight is in the evening. The airport has a small food court with affordable options. Don't forget to use any remaining TheBus passes. Mahalo for visiting Hawaii — leave only footprints!

trip_options.title: Classic Hawaii Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Daniel K. Inouye International Airport at 13:00. Collect luggage, pick up rental car, and drive ~20 minutes to Hanauma Bay, East Oahu Boutique Stay. Check in, unpack, and freshen up. Take a leisurely stroll along the nearby coastline to get your first glimpse of the Pacific Ocean and orient yourselves with the neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed welcome dinner at a nearby local restaurant. Head to Kona Brewing Company in Hawaii Kai (~10 min drive) for casual, family-friendly dining with fresh seafood, wood-fired pizzas, and locally crafted beverages with ocean views.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport upon arrival
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the airport or a nearby café like Zippy's (local Hawaiian comfort food chain) on the drive to the hotel
meals.dinner: Kona Brewing Company, Hawaii Kai — mid-range, family-friendly, great local atmosphere (~$20–35/person)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light and stress-free. Jet lag may be a factor depending on origin. Pick up a rental car at the airport — it's essential for exploring Oahu. Stock up on snacks and drinks at a nearby Foodland or Times Supermarket for the room.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay — just minutes from your hotel, this is the perfect first full-day activity. Arrive early (7:00–8:00 AM) to beat the crowds and secure entry. Watch the mandatory marine education video, then spend 2–3 hours snorkeling among hundreds of tropical fish in the protected bay. Rent snorkel gear on-site if needed (~$15/person).
day_by_day.afternoon: After Hanauma Bay, drive to nearby Sandy Beach Park (~5 min) to relax on the sand, watch local bodyboarders, and enjoy the rugged east-side scenery. Continue along the scenic Kalanianaole Highway to Makapuu Lookout for stunning panoramic views of the windward coast — a short 0.5-mile paved walk to the lighthouse viewpoint.
day_by_day.evening: Head back toward Hawaii Kai for dinner. Try Nico's Pier 38 or drive slightly further to Kaimana Beach area near Waikiki for a sunset dinner at the Hau Tree Restaurant — a beloved open-air spot with affordable Hawaiian-inspired cuisine right on the beach.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel or pack granola bars and fruit to eat before Hanauma Bay opens
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch — pack sandwiches and snacks from the supermarket, or grab plate lunches from a nearby L&L Hawaiian Barbecue
meals.dinner: Hau Tree Restaurant at Kaimana Beach Hotel — casual, scenic, mid-range (~$25–40/person)

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay requires advance reservations online (book at least 2–3 days ahead at hawaiistateparks.reserveamerica.com). Entry fee is ~$25/adult, children under 13 free. Bring reef-safe sunscreen — it's required by Hawaii state law.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Waikiki (~25 min from hotel) for Surfing Lessons at Waikiki Beach. Book a 2-hour beginner group lesson with a certified local instructor — Waikiki's gentle, rolling waves make it the best place in the world to learn. Most schools (Hans Hedemann Surf School, Aloha Beach Services) include board and rash guard rental. Kids as young as 5 can participate.
day_by_day.afternoon: After surfing, spend the afternoon exploring Waikiki. Walk along Kalakaua Avenue, browse the International Market Place (open-air shopping mall), and cool off with shave ice from Island Vintage Shave Ice inside the mall. Visit the Waikiki Aquarium (~$12/adult) for a family-friendly deep dive into Hawaiian marine life.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Waikiki for dinner before heading back to the hotel. Enjoy dinner at Duke's Waikiki — a legendary beachfront restaurant named after Duke Kahanamoku, serving fresh fish, burgers, and Hawaiian classics with live music most evenings.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before driving to Waikiki — toast, fruit, yogurt, or a quick stop at a local café
meals.lunch: Grab a quick plate lunch near Waikiki Beach at Ono Seafood or a food truck on Kapahulu Avenue (~$10–15/person)
meals.dinner: Duke's Waikiki on the Beach — iconic, mid-range, lively atmosphere (~$25–45/person)

day_by_day.notes: Book surfing lessons in advance, especially in August (peak season). Most lessons are 1.5–2 hours and cost ~$50–75/person for group lessons. Apply waterproof reef-safe sunscreen before hitting the water. Parking in Waikiki can be expensive — use the International Market Place garage or find street parking further inland.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to the North Shore (~1 hour from hotel) for the Shave Ice and Local Food Tour in Haleiwa. Start by exploring the charming surf town of Haleiwa — browse local boutiques, surf shops, and galleries. Stop at Matsumoto Shave Ice (the most famous on the island) for Hawaii's iconic treat with tropical flavors and mochi or azuki bean toppings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the North Shore. Visit Waimea Bay Beach Park for swimming and cliff jumping (seasonal — safe in summer when waves are calm). Drive to Sunset Beach and Ehukai Beach Park (home of the famous Banzai Pipeline) to walk the shore and watch local surfers. Stop at Ted's Bakery near Sunset Beach for a legendary chocolate haupia cream pie slice.
day_by_day.evening: Head back toward the hotel via the Kamehameha Highway and Pali Highway scenic route. Stop for dinner in Kaneohe or Kailua on the windward side — try Buzz's Original Steakhouse in Kailua, a beloved local institution with steaks, fresh fish, and salad bar in a relaxed setting.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel before the drive, or stop at Café Haleiwa in town — a classic North Shore surfer breakfast spot
meals.lunch: Local food tour style — shave ice at Matsumoto's, garlic shrimp from Giovanni's Shrimp Truck (a must-do North Shore experience, ~$15/plate)
meals.dinner: Buzz's Original Steakhouse, Kailua — casual, mid-range, local favorite (~$30–50/person)

day_by_day.notes: Giovanni's Shrimp Truck is parked in Kahuku — a short drive past Haleiwa heading north. It's cash-friendly and iconic. August is summer in Hawaii so North Shore waves are small and calm — ideal for swimming at Waimea Bay. The drive along the North Shore is one of Oahu's most scenic routes.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Polynesian Cultural Center (PCC) in Laie on the North Shore (~45 min from hotel). Arrive when it opens (11:30 AM) to explore the six authentic Polynesian village exhibits representing Hawaii, Samoa, Aotearoa (New Zealand), Fiji, Tonga, and Tahiti. Participate in hands-on cultural demonstrations — coconut husking, fire making, tapa cloth making, and traditional canoe rides.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the PCC villages in the afternoon. Catch the afternoon canoe pageant on the lagoon — a colorful, free-flowing parade of traditional Polynesian canoes with performers in full cultural regalia. This is a highlight for families and runs daily around 2:30 PM.
day_by_day.evening: Stay at PCC for the Luau Dinner at the Polynesian Cultural Center — a spectacular beachfront luau experience with an imu (underground oven) ceremony, traditional Hawaiian foods (kalua pig, poi, lomi salmon, haupia), and the breathtaking Ha: Breath of Life evening show featuring 100+ performers with fire dancing and Polynesian music.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — fuel up before a full day at PCC
meals.lunch: Lunch inside the PCC at the Pounders Restaurant (buffet-style Hawaiian and Polynesian foods, included in some packages) or the Gateway Bar & Grill
meals.dinner: Ali'i Luau at the Polynesian Cultural Center — included in the luau package (~$120–160/adult, ~$80–100/child, book in advance)

day_by_day.notes: Book PCC tickets and the luau package well in advance at polynesia.com — August is peak season and luau spots sell out. The full-day package including the luau and evening show is the best value. Plan to spend 6–8 hours at PCC. It is operated by Brigham Young University–Hawaii, so no alcohol is served on the premises.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning after the big PCC day. Sleep in, enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast, and spend the morning at the hotel pool or take a gentle walk along the coastline near Hanauma Bay. This is a great time to do laundry, recharge devices, and plan the second half of the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Kailua Beach on the windward side (~20 min from hotel) — consistently rated one of the best beaches in the US. The powdery white sand and turquoise calm waters are perfect for families. Rent kayaks or stand-up paddleboards from Kailua Beach Adventures (~$60–80 for a double kayak) and paddle out to the Mokulua Islands offshore.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in the charming Kailua town — walk along Kailua Road and choose from a variety of restaurants. Try Cinnamon's at the Ilima Hotel for a beloved local dinner, or head to Kalapawai Market & Deli for casual gourmet sandwiches, salads, and local wines in a relaxed setting.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast or nearby café
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic for Kailua Beach — grab supplies from Whole Foods or Kalapawai Market in Kailua town
meals.dinner: Kalapawai Market & Deli, Kailua — casual, mid-range, local favorite (~$15–25/person)

day_by_day.notes: Kailua Beach has no lifeguards, but conditions are generally very calm in summer — perfect for families. Arrive by early afternoon to get a good parking spot (free parking lot fills up). The paddle to the Mokulua Islands takes about 30–45 minutes each way and is suitable for beginners in calm conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning hike to Diamond Head State Monument (~20 min drive from hotel). This iconic 1.6-mile round-trip hike climbs inside a volcanic crater to a stunning 360-degree panoramic view of Waikiki, Honolulu, and the Pacific. Start by 7:00–8:00 AM to beat the heat and crowds. The hike takes about 1.5 hours round-trip and is suitable for older children.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Waikiki for an afternoon at the beach — swim, build sandcastles, and soak in the famous Waikiki atmosphere. Visit the Bishop Museum of Hawaii (a short drive inland, ~$25/adult) if the family prefers a cultural afternoon — it houses the world's largest collection of Hawaiian and Pacific artifacts and has an engaging planetarium.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sunset dinner in Waikiki. Try the House Without a Key at the Halekulani Hotel — an iconic open-air lounge and restaurant with live Hawaiian music, hula dancing, and beautiful sunset views over the ocean. Order fresh fish, pupus (appetizers), and tropical cocktails (or mocktails for kids).

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast before the Diamond Head hike — granola bars, bananas, and plenty of water
meals.lunch: Lunch near Waikiki — try Marukame Udon on Kalakaua Avenue for delicious, affordable Japanese-Hawaiian udon noodles (~$8–12/person, expect a line)
meals.dinner: House Without a Key, Halekulani Hotel — upscale casual, mid-to-upper range (~$30–55/person), reserve in advance

day_by_day.notes: Diamond Head requires advance reservations at gostateparks.hawaii.gov — entry is $5/person. Wear sturdy shoes and bring water. The hike involves some steep stairs and a tunnel. Not recommended for very young toddlers. Marukame Udon is extremely popular — go before noon or after 2 PM to avoid long lines.

day_by_day.morning: Spend a final relaxed morning snorkeling at Hanauma Bay again (or exploring the tide pools along the east coast near your hotel). Alternatively, visit Lanai Lookout and the Halona Blowhole (~5 min from hotel) — a dramatic natural lava tube that shoots seawater into the air. Check the small cove below (From Here to Eternity Beach) for a secluded swimming spot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Sea Life Park Hawaii in Waimanalo (~15 min from hotel) — a family-favorite marine park featuring dolphin encounters, sea turtle interactions, penguin feedings, and Hawaiian monk seal exhibits. Dolphin swim programs are available for an additional fee and are a once-in-a-lifetime family experience (book well in advance).
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate the near-end of your trip with a special dinner. Drive to Honolulu's Chinatown or Kakaako neighborhood (~25 min) for a more eclectic dining experience. Try Livestock Tavern in Chinatown for upscale farm-to-table Hawaiian cuisine, or MW Restaurant for a celebrated local chef's take on Hawaii Regional Cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or pick up fresh pastries and coffee from a local café
meals.lunch: Lunch at Sea Life Park's on-site café, or pack a lunch to enjoy at the park
meals.dinner: MW Restaurant, Honolulu — upscale mid-range, local celebrity chefs Wade Ueoka and Michelle Karr-Ueoka (~$40–60/person, reservations recommended)

day_by_day.notes: Sea Life Park admission is ~$40/adult, ~$25/child. Dolphin swim experiences are an additional ~$150–250/person and must be booked in advance. The park is small enough to see everything in 3–4 hours. Halona Blowhole is best viewed on days with some wave activity — the viewing area is free and takes only 15–20 minutes.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the USS Arizona Memorial and Pearl Harbor Historic Sites (~35 min drive from hotel). This deeply moving and historically significant site includes the free USS Arizona Memorial (requires timed entry reservation at recreation.gov), the Battleship Missouri, the Pacific Aviation Museum, and the USS Bowfin submarine. Plan to spend at least half a day here.
day_by_day.afternoon: After Pearl Harbor, drive to the Aloha Tower Marketplace on Honolulu's historic waterfront for lunch and souvenir shopping. Browse the stalls for locally made gifts, Hawaiian clothing, macadamia nut products, and Kona coffee. Then head to Ala Moana Center — Hawaii's largest open-air shopping mall — for any last-minute shopping and people-watching.
day_by_day.evening: Final beach sunset at Ala Moana Beach Park, adjacent to the shopping center — a beautiful, locals-favorite beach with calm waters, picnic areas, and stunning sunset views. End the evening with a farewell dinner nearby at Mariposa Restaurant inside Neiman Marcus at Ala Moana — known for its beautiful lanai views and refined Hawaiian-influenced cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before driving to Pearl Harbor
meals.lunch: Lunch at Aloha Tower Marketplace — Gordon Biersch Brewery Restaurant offers solid mid-range American and Hawaiian dishes with harbor views (~$20–30/person)
meals.dinner: Mariposa Restaurant, Ala Moana Center — upscale casual, mid-to-upper range (~$35–55/person, reservations recommended)

day_by_day.notes: Pearl Harbor is one of Oahu's most visited sites — book USS Arizona Memorial tickets as far in advance as possible (they're free but timed). Allow 4–5 hours if visiting multiple attractions. The Battleship Missouri and Pacific Aviation Museum charge separate admission (~$30–35/adult each). Expect emotional and reflective moments — this is a powerful experience for families.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Hawaii — wake up early for one last sunrise walk along the coastline near Hanauma Bay. Take photos, collect a few small shells as memories (no coral or live shells), and breathe in the ocean air. Return to the hotel for a final breakfast and begin packing and checking out.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hotel and drive to the airport (~25 min). Return the rental car (allow extra time for this process). Arrive at Daniel K. Inouye International Airport at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for international departures or 2 hours for domestic. Browse the airport's local food and souvenir shops — Honolulu Cookie Company and Island Vintage Coffee are great last-minute picks.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Hawaii with wonderful memories, a tan, and a suitcase full of macadamia nuts and aloha spirit.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — savor it! Or walk to a nearby café for one last local meal
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the hotel before checkout, or grab food at the airport — Panda Express, local plate lunch options, or a sit-down meal at one of the airport restaurants
meals.dinner: On the plane or at your connecting airport

day_by_day.notes: Check your flight time carefully and plan checkout and airport drive accordingly. Most Oahu hotels have a 11:00 AM checkout — ask for a late checkout if your flight is in the evening. Leave time to return the rental car and shuttle to the terminal. Honolulu Airport has a nice selection of local food and gift shops post-security. Mahalo for a wonderful trip!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Hawaii Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Hanauma Bay, East Oahu Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay
experiences.description: Explore one of Hawaii's most pristine marine sanctuaries with crystal-clear waters teeming with tropical fish and sea turtles. Perfect for families with kids of all ages, the bay offers calm, shallow waters and equipment rentals on-site. An educational orientation video is required before entering, making it a fun learning experience for the whole family.

experiences.name: Luau Dinner at Polynesian Cultural Center
experiences.description: Immerse your family in authentic Hawaiian and Polynesian culture with a spectacular beachfront luau featuring traditional hula dancing, fire knife performances, and an all-you-can-eat feast of local Hawaiian cuisine including kalua pig, poi, and fresh tropical fruits. A memorable cultural evening for the entire family.

experiences.name: Surfing Lessons at Waikiki Beach
experiences.description: Take beginner-friendly surfing lessons right on the iconic Waikiki shoreline with certified local instructors. The gentle rolling waves of Waikiki make it the perfect spot for first-timers and kids. Group lessons are available for families, and most participants are standing on a board within the first hour. Boards and rash guards are included.

experiences.name: Shave Ice and Local Food Tour in Haleiwa
experiences.description: Stroll through the charming beachside town of Haleiwa on the North Shore and indulge in Hawaii's most beloved treat — rainbow shave ice topped with local syrups and mochi. Sample fresh poke bowls, garlic shrimp from roadside trucks, and tropical smoothies. A delicious and affordable way to taste authentic Hawaiian flavors as a family.

experiences.name: Whale Watching Cruise from Maalaea Harbor
experiences.description: Embark on a family-friendly whale watching boat tour during peak humpback whale season off the coast of Maui. Knowledgeable naturalist guides narrate the experience as you witness majestic humpback whales breaching and tail-slapping just offshore. Many tours offer a money-back guarantee if no whales are spotted. Life jackets and snacks are provided on board.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Flight LH lands; clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange private luxury transfer to Hanauma Bay, East Oahu Boutique Stay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private check-in experience at the boutique property. Settle into your suite, enjoy a welcome amenity (tropical fruit platter and mai tais), then take a leisurely stroll along the shoreline near Hanauma Bay to get your bearings and breathe in the ocean air.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed first-night dinner at the hotel's signature restaurant or a nearby acclaimed spot such as 3660 On the Rise (Kaimuki) — a beloved Oahu fine-dining institution known for Euro-Island cuisine, fresh local fish, and an award-winning wine list. Early night to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: In-flight or airport lounge meal before landing
meals.lunch: Light welcome spread arranged by the hotel upon arrival
meals.dinner: 3660 On the Rise, Kaimuki — reserve the chef's tasting menu with wine pairing for a premium first-night experience

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange a private luxury SUV transfer from Honolulu International Airport. Confirm early check-in with the boutique property. Keep Day 1 light — jet lag is real, especially for families traveling long-haul.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay — your hotel's prime location makes this a perfect short walk or quick ride away. Arrive early (7:30–8:00 AM) to beat crowds and secure the best marine viewing conditions. Book a private guided snorkel tour with premium equipment rental for the family; a certified naturalist guide will introduce you to sea turtles, parrotfish, and vibrant coral formations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel for a poolside lunch, then enjoy a private family surf lesson at a calm nearby beach cove arranged through the hotel's concierge. Alternatively, relax at the hotel's infinity pool with ocean views.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on your private lanai or the hotel's rooftop terrace, followed by dinner at Vintage Cave Honolulu — one of Hawaii's most exclusive and celebrated fine-dining restaurants offering an extraordinary multi-course tasting menu in a stunning underground setting.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast service — eggs Benedict, fresh tropical fruit, Kona coffee, and fresh-pressed juices
meals.lunch: Poolside dining at the hotel — grilled mahi-mahi tacos, acai bowls, and fresh coconut water
meals.dinner: Vintage Cave Honolulu — advance reservation essential; expect a 10-course chef's tasting menu with sommelier-paired wines

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay requires advance online reservations; book at least 2 weeks prior. The bay is closed on Tuesdays. First-time visitors must watch a short marine education video before entering. Bring reef-safe sunscreen only — standard sunscreen is banned to protect coral.

day_by_day.morning: Since Hanauma Bay is closed on Tuesdays, head to Kailua Beach — consistently rated one of America's most beautiful beaches. Arrange a private beachside setup through a luxury concierge service (umbrella, chaise lounges, chilled towels, and a cooler of refreshments). Enjoy calm, turquoise waters perfect for families. Rent kayaks or stand-up paddleboards for a leisurely paddle to the Mokulua Islands.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive up to the Nuuanu Pali Lookout for dramatic panoramic views of the Windward Coast, then visit the Byodo-In Temple in the Valley of the Temples — a stunning replica of a 900-year-old Japanese temple set against lush Ko'olau Mountains. A peaceful and visually spectacular family experience.
day_by_day.evening: Luau Dinner at the Polynesian Cultural Center — an immersive, world-class cultural experience featuring authentic performances from Hawaii, Samoa, Tonga, Fiji, Tahiti, and New Zealand. Upgrade to the Ali'i Luau package for premium front-row seating, a dedicated server, and a lavish feast.

meals.breakfast: Hotel restaurant — loco moco with wagyu beef patty, eggs, and rich brown gravy; a true Hawaiian breakfast staple
meals.lunch: Buzz's Original Steakhouse in Kailua — a beloved local institution with fresh catch, burgers, and cold drinks steps from the beach
meals.dinner: Ali'i Luau at Polynesian Cultural Center — all-inclusive feast with kalua pig, poi, haupia, tropical fruits, and unlimited beverages

day_by_day.notes: The Polynesian Cultural Center is approximately 35–40 minutes from Hanauma Bay. Arrange a private luxury van for the family. The luau begins at sunset — arrive 30 minutes early for prime photo opportunities at the oceanfront fire ceremony.

day_by_day.morning: Surfing Lessons at Waikiki Beach — take the family for beginner-friendly group or private surfing lessons with certified local instructors on the world's most iconic surf break. Waikiki's gentle rolling waves are ideal for first-timers. Book a private 2-hour lesson for the entire family through a premium surf school for personalized attention.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Waikiki and the broader Honolulu area. Visit the Bishop Museum — Hawaii's premier natural and cultural history museum — for an enriching family experience covering Hawaiian royalty, volcanology, and Pacific Island cultures. Alternatively, browse the luxury boutiques along Kalakaua Avenue (Chanel, Louis Vuitton, Tiffany & Co.).
day_by_day.evening: Sunset dinner cruise departing from Ala Moana Harbor aboard a luxury catamaran. Enjoy champagne, premium pupus (appetizers), and a gourmet dinner while watching the sun dip behind Diamond Head. Many operators offer live Hawaiian music and hula performance on board.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — macadamia nut pancakes with coconut syrup, fresh papaya, and Kona espresso
meals.lunch: Nobu Honolulu at Waikiki Beach Marriott — world-renowned Japanese-Peruvian fusion; try the black cod miso and yellowtail jalapeño
meals.dinner: Luxury sunset dinner cruise — gourmet catered meal with open premium bar, fresh island fish, and tropical desserts

day_by_day.notes: Waikiki is approximately 20–25 minutes from Hanauma Bay. Book surf lessons at least a week in advance for private family sessions. For the dinner cruise, bring a light layer — ocean breezes can be cool after sunset.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Hanauma Bay for a second snorkeling session — this time explore the deeper outer reef with a private dive guide if family members are certified divers, or continue snorkeling in the inner bay. The early morning light creates spectacular underwater visibility. Spot octopus, eels, and rare Hawaiian state fish (humuhumunukunukuapua'a).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Diamond Head State Monument for a family hike to the summit crater. The 1.6-mile round-trip trail offers spectacular 360-degree views of Honolulu, Waikiki, and the Pacific Ocean. Book a private guided hiking experience with a local naturalist who will share the history of this iconic volcanic tuff cone.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Mama's Fish House (requires advance planning — it's on Maui, so this evening could instead feature a special in-room private chef experience). Book a private chef through the hotel's concierge to prepare a full Hawaiian feast in your suite — fresh poke, grilled opakapaka, haupia dessert — with a curated wine selection.

meals.breakfast: In-room continental breakfast — fresh-baked pastries, tropical fruit, Greek yogurt with local honey, and cold brew coffee
meals.lunch: Roy's Restaurant, Hawaii Kai — just minutes from Hanauma Bay; James Beard Award-winning chef Roy Yamaguchi's flagship offering Hawaiian fusion cuisine with stunning ocean views
meals.dinner: Private in-suite chef experience — a 5-course Hawaiian tasting menu prepared tableside with wine pairing; coordinate through hotel concierge 48 hours in advance

day_by_day.notes: Diamond Head hike is moderately easy but involves stairs and uneven terrain. Start no later than 4:00 PM to enjoy the golden-hour summit views. Bring water and sun protection. The private chef experience requires 48-hour advance booking through the hotel.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the North Shore — depart early for the legendary surf mecca of Oahu's North Shore. Visit Sunset Beach and Ehukai Beach Park (home of the famous Banzai Pipeline). In August the waves are calm and perfect for swimming, making it ideal for families. Enjoy a pristine, uncrowded beach morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Shave Ice and Local Food Tour in Haleiwa — stroll through the charming, colorful surf town of Haleiwa. Stop at Matsumoto Shave Ice (a North Shore institution since 1951) for the iconic Hawaiian treat with azuki beans and mochi. Explore local art galleries, boutiques, and farm-to-table food stalls. Visit Ted's Bakery for legendary chocolate haupia cream pie.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Haleiwa Joe's Haiku Gardens (on the way back toward Honolulu side) or return to the Honolulu area for dinner at Senia — a critically acclaimed modern American restaurant with inventive tasting menus using the finest local Hawaiian ingredients. James Beard Award nominated.

meals.breakfast: Early grab-and-go breakfast from the hotel — smoothie packs, granola bars, and cold brew for the drive
meals.lunch: Giovanni's Shrimp Truck in Kahuku — a legendary North Shore food truck institution; the scampi shrimp plate is world-famous and a true bucket-list food experience
meals.dinner: Senia Restaurant, Honolulu — chef's counter tasting menu experience with hyper-local Hawaiian ingredients; reserve well in advance

day_by_day.notes: The North Shore is approximately 45–55 minutes from Hanauma Bay. Depart by 8:00 AM to enjoy the beach before midday crowds. The Haleiwa food tour is self-guided but can be arranged with a private food tour guide for a more curated experience.

day_by_day.morning: Private helicopter tour of Oahu — one of the most spectacular luxury experiences available in Hawaii. Depart from Honolulu Airport for a 45–60-minute private doors-off helicopter tour covering Diamond Head, the Ko'olau Mountains, Sacred Falls, Chinaman's Hat, and the stunning Windward Coast. Absolutely breathtaking for the whole family.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the USS Arizona Memorial and Pearl Harbor National Memorial — a profoundly moving and historically significant experience. Book a premium VIP guided tour that bypasses general queues and includes a private historian guide. Essential for older children and adults.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell-to-Honolulu dinner at Orchids Restaurant at the Halekulani Hotel — one of Oahu's most iconic fine-dining venues with unobstructed ocean views, white-glove service, and an exceptional menu of Pacific Rim cuisine. Sunday brunch here is legendary, but the dinner service is equally exquisite.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — eggs any style, smoked salmon, avocado toast with ahi poke, fresh-squeezed lilikoi juice
meals.lunch: Nico's Pier 38 near the harbor — fresh-off-the-boat fish, premium poke bowls, and local plate lunches in a relaxed waterfront setting
meals.dinner: Orchids at Halekulani Hotel — prix-fixe dinner with tableside service, fresh island fish, and a world-class wine cellar selection

day_by_day.notes: Book the helicopter tour at least 2 weeks in advance; doors-off tours require weight and age considerations for safety. Pearl Harbor requires advance timed-entry reservations — book online as soon as possible. The memorial is free but the premium VIP tour is a paid upgrade worth every penny.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise yoga and meditation session on the beach arranged by the hotel's wellness concierge. A certified instructor leads a private 75-minute session on the sand at Hanauma Bay as the sun rises over the Pacific — a transformative and rejuvenating family experience. Follow with a refreshing morning swim.
day_by_day.afternoon: Sea Life Park Hawaii — a fantastic family-friendly marine park located just minutes from Hanauma Bay on the Windward Coast. Enjoy dolphin encounters, sea turtle feeding, Hawaiian monk seal exhibits, and snorkeling lagoons. Book the premium 'Dolphin Royal Swim' experience for an unforgettable close-up dolphin interaction.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at Makapuu Lookout — one of Oahu's most dramatic coastal viewpoints just minutes away. Watch for spinner dolphins in the waters below. Then enjoy a relaxed, intimate dinner at Kona Brewing Company's Koko Marina location — casual but excellent, with craft beers, fresh pizzas, and island-inspired dishes in a marina setting.

meals.breakfast: Post-yoga brunch at the hotel — acai bowls, smashed avocado toast with poached eggs, and a fresh tropical fruit platter
meals.lunch: Sea Life Park's premium dining area — pack a gourmet picnic basket arranged by the hotel's concierge for a beachside family lunch
meals.dinner: Kona Brewing Company, Koko Marina (Hawaii Kai) — relaxed waterfront dining; try the fresh catch fish and chips and the Longboard Island Lager

day_by_day.notes: Sea Life Park is approximately 10 minutes from Hanauma Bay — extremely convenient. The Dolphin Royal Swim must be booked well in advance and has age/height requirements. The sunrise yoga session should be arranged through the hotel concierge the evening before.

day_by_day.morning: Private catamaran sailing charter — depart from Hawaii Kai Marina (minutes from the hotel) for a private half-day luxury sailing experience along the stunning southeastern Oahu coastline. Sail past Koko Head, Hanauma Bay from the ocean, and Sandy Beach. Enjoy snorkeling stops, freshly prepared breakfast on deck, and premium champagne.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Honolulu Museum of Art — one of the finest art museums in the Pacific, housing an extraordinary collection of Asian, European, and Pacific art. The Spanish Courtyard and café are particularly beautiful. A culturally enriching afternoon for the whole family. Follow with a final luxury shopping session in the Ala Moana Center.
day_by_day.evening: Penultimate night celebration dinner at MW Restaurant, Honolulu — helmed by James Beard Award-winning chefs Wade Ueoka and Michelle Karr-Ueoka. The restaurant masterfully blends local Hawaiian ingredients with Japanese and European techniques. The dessert program is extraordinary.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast served on the private catamaran deck — smoked salmon bagels, tropical fruit, mimosas, and freshly brewed Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Honolulu Museum of Art Café — light Mediterranean-inspired lunch in the stunning courtyard setting
meals.dinner: MW Restaurant, Honolulu — seasonal tasting menu with wine pairing; the mochi cake dessert is legendary

day_by_day.notes: Private catamaran charters from Hawaii Kai Marina can be arranged through the hotel concierge or directly with operators like Ko Olina Catamaran Charters. Half-day charters typically run 4–5 hours. Book the MW Restaurant reservation at least 2 weeks in advance — it is consistently one of Honolulu's most sought-after tables.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at Hanauma Bay — one last sunrise snorkel session in this magical marine sanctuary. Collect shells, take final photos, and soak in the extraordinary beauty of this place. Return to the hotel for a luxurious farewell breakfast and begin packing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time, enjoy a final poolside afternoon at the hotel with cocktails and light bites. Visit the hotel spa for a relaxing traditional lomilomi massage — Hawaii's signature healing massage using long, flowing strokes that mirror the movement of ocean waves. A perfect send-off for the whole family.
day_by_day.evening: Private transfer to Honolulu International Airport. Farewell dinner, if time permits before departure, at the airport's premium dining options or arrange a to-go gourmet picnic from the hotel featuring local delicacies: fresh poke, macadamia nut chocolates, Kona coffee, and Hawaiian sea salt caramels as edible souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at the hotel — full Hawaiian spread including laulau, poi, fresh poke, tropical fruits, macadamia nut waffles, and Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Poolside light lunch — fresh ceviche, shrimp cocktail, and a final round of mai tais
meals.dinner: Hotel-prepared gourmet departure picnic box or airport lounge dining — premium sandwiches, local snacks, and beverages for the journey home

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private luxury airport transfer at least 3 hours before international departure. The hotel can prepare a custom farewell gift bag with local Hawaiian products — Kona coffee, macadamia nuts, Hawaiian sea salt, and local honey. Lomilomi spa sessions should be booked the evening before. Check airline baggage allowances if purchasing local goods to bring home.
